theorem_title: The finite coloring driver decides distinct-index 3SUM
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightThreeSumFastDriver.program_meets {lim : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Limits} {colorProgram : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Program} {pColor : ℕ}
    {colorNeed : ℕ→ℕ→_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Need} {src n free U colorTime d : ℕ}
    (x : Fin n→ℤ) (μ : ℕ→ℤ)
    (H : (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.ThreeSumColorDriverResources.fullNeed colorNeed n U).Ok lim free d)
    (hsrc : src+n≤free) (hinput : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Seg μ src (List.ofFn x))
    (hcolor : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightThreeSumColorDriver.ColorLaw lim colorProgram pColor colorNeed
      src n free (_root_.ThreeSum.LightThreeSumFastDriver.row free) U colorTime x) :
    _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Meets lim (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightThreeSumFastDriver.program colorProgram pColor) (colorProgram.length+26) d [src,n,free] μ (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightThreeSumFastDriver.time colorTime n)
      (fun r ξ => (r=0 ∨ r=1) ∧ (r=1 ↔ _root_.ThreeSum.Coloring.DistinctZeroSum x) ∧ _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Kept μ ξ free) := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $x$ be a length-$n$ integer input stored before a free pointer. Suppose a concrete color program and entry procedure satisfy the stated color law with resource function and per-color time, and the complete driver resource predicate holds. The assembled fast driver, entered at procedure $|P_{\mathrm{color}}|+26$, returns a Boolean equivalent to the existence of three distinct indices with zero sum, preserves earlier memory, and meets its exact finite-color time bound.

This driver theorem promotes a concrete per-color execution law to an exact original-input 3SUM decision.
